types.name: Query
types.description: The root query type which gives access points into the data universe.

fields.name: query
fields.description:
Exposes the root query type nested one level down. This is helpful for Relay 1
which can only query top level fields if they are in a particular form.

fields.name: nodeId
fields.description: The root query type must be a `Node` to work well with Relay 1 mutations. This just resolves to `query`.

fields.name: node
fields.description: Fetches an object given its globally unique `ID`.

args.name: nodeId
args.description: The globally unique `ID`.

types.name: Node
types.description: An object with a globally unique `ID`.

fields.name: nodeId
fields.description: A globally unique identifier. Can be used in various places throughout the system to identify this single value.

types.name: ID
types.description: The `ID` scalar type represents a unique identifier, often used to refetch an object or as key for a cache. The ID type appears in a JSON response as a String; however, it is not intended to be human-readable. When expected as an input type, any string (such as `"4"`) or integer (such as `4`) input value will be accepted as an ID.

types.name: AccountBalancesConnection
types.description: A connection to a list of `AccountBalance` values.

fields.name: nodes
fields.description: A list of `AccountBalance` objects.

fields.name: edges
fields.description: A list of edges which contains the `AccountBalance` and cursor to aid in pagination.

fields.name: pageInfo
fields.description: Information to aid in pagination.

fields.name: totalCount
fields.description: The count of *all* `AccountBalance` you could get from the connection.

fields.name: aggregates
fields.description: Aggregates across the matching connection (ignoring before/after/first/last/offset)

fields.name: groupedAggregates
fields.description: Grouped aggregates across the matching connection (ignoring before/after/first/last/offset)

args.name: groupBy
args.description: The method to use when grouping `AccountBalance` for these aggregates.

args.name: having
args.description: Conditions on the grouped aggregates.

fields.name: nodeId
fields.description: A globally unique identifier. Can be used in various places throughout the system to identify this single value.

fields.name: id
fields.description: address

fields.name: frozen
fields.description: MAX over active locks — maintained from `locks`, never summed

fields.name: transferable
fields.description: free - frozen, floored at 0

fields.name: bonded
fields.description: the staking lock: bonded plus unbonding, until withdrawn. Its unbonding chunks are `staking.ledger(controller).unlocking`

fields.name: totalReceived
fields.description: lifetime totals — free, this row is already versioned on these blocks

fields.name: totalFeesPaid
fields.description: Lifetime fees, net of refunds. From v8 it leaves out a fee that was not taken by a withdrawal of its own: an Ethereum transaction's fee, or one paid from withdrawals that also covered contract deposits. Its POLYX is in `Burn` entries, so the balance is right

fields.name: locks
fields.description: per-lock detail — required because frozen is a MAX

fields.name: holds
fields.description: v8 only; SUM = reserved

fields.name: account
fields.description: Reads a single `Account` that is related to this `AccountBalance`.

fields.name: identity
fields.description: Reads a single `Identity` that is related to this `AccountBalance`.

fields.name: updatedEvent
fields.description: Reads a single `Event` that is related to this `AccountBalance`.

types.name: String
types.description: The `String` scalar type represents textual data, represented as UTF-8 character sequences. The String type is most often used by GraphQL to represent free-form human-readable text.

types.name: BigFloat
types.description: A floating point number that requires more precision than IEEE 754 binary 64

types.name: Int
types.description: The `Int` scalar type represents non-fractional signed whole numeric values. Int can represent values between -(2^31) and 2^31 - 1.

types.name: JSON
types.description: The `JSON` scalar type represents JSON values as specified by [ECMA-404](http://www.ecma-international.org/publications/files/ECMA-ST/ECMA-404.pdf).

fields.name: nodeId
fields.description: A globally unique identifier. Can be used in various places throughout the system to identify this single value.

fields.name: keyType
fields.description: `substrate` for a regular key, `ethereum` for the `0xEE` padded account of an Ethereum key

fields.name: keyRole
fields.description: The key's current role, derived from the chain's `KeyRecord`. A convenience column: the membership history it summarises is `keyAssignments`

fields.name: evmAddress
fields.description: Checksummed Ethereum address this account is reachable at inside `pallet_revive`

fields.name: identityId
fields.description: The identity this key currently belongs to, null once it is detached. A convenience column for the current state; `keyAssignments` is the authoritative membership record, including past ones

fields.name: identity
fields.description: Reads a single `Identity` that is related to this `Account`.

fields.name: createdEvent
fields.description: Reads a single `Event` that is related to this `Account`.

fields.name: updatedEvent
fields.description: Reads a single `Event` that is related to this `Account`.

types.name: AccountKeyRole
types.description:
The role a key plays in the identity system, from the chain's own `KeyRecord`.

Distinct from `Account.keyType` (the cryptographic shape of the key). Treated as an OPEN set —
`Unlinked` currently covers pallet addresses, system pots, and deliberately-detached keys as one
label, and may be split later. A multisig's own account reads `PrimaryKey` / `SecondaryKey` per
its key record; multisig-ness is the `MultiSig` row keyed by the same address, not this field.

A superset of `IdentityKeyRole`: a key can sit outside the identity system entirely, which a
membership interval cannot express. The values common to both are spelled the same way.

fields.name: datetime
fields.description:
Block timestamp. UTC — but this applies to EVERY `Date`/`datetime` field in the API:
SubQuery types `Date` as Postgres `timestamp without time zone`, so it is serialised
with no zone marker (`"2021-11-05T13:56:36"`). A consumer calling `new Date(value)`
in most runtimes gets *local* time, shifting it silently by its own offset. Parse
every datetime as UTC — `new Date(value + 'Z')`, or `dayjs.utc(value)`.

fields.name: success
fields.description: `1` when the extrinsic itself succeeded. A `utility` batch that stops at a failing call, or a `force_batch` that skips failing calls, still succeeds as an extrinsic, so this says nothing about the calls inside it: use `batchFailed`

fields.name: batchFailed
fields.description: `true` when a batch inside this extrinsic reported a failed call: `BatchInterrupted`, `BatchInterruptedOld`, `BatchOptimisticFailed`, `BatchCompletedWithErrors` or `ItemFailed` is among its `events`, including a batch nested in a wrapper such as a multisig execution, a relayed call, `as_derivative` or a committee execution. `false` for every other extrinsic, a batch that fully succeeded included, and for an extrinsic that failed as a whole (check `success` first: a `batch_all` that fails reverts everything, so `success` is `0` and this is `false`). A failed `relay_tx` or `dispatch_as` inner call is not flagged. Before v7 a `batch_atomic` that fails reports `BatchInterruptedOld` although its changes were rolled back, so this is `true` there with nothing applied. Not indexed: combine a filter on it with an indexed one

fields.name: creatorId
fields.description:
The identity that dispatched `create_multisig` (the `MultiSigCreated` event's `callerDid`).

NULL for a multisig that existed at genesis: the chain keeps no `creator` storage (only
`multiSig.adminDid` and `multiSig.payingDid`), so for a row not observed being created the
creator is unrecoverable. Do NOT read this as "who controls it" — that is `admins`, which is
mutable (`multiSig.adminDid`, changed via `add_admin` / `remove_admin`) — nor as "which identity
it acts for", which is `account.identity` (the multisig joined to an identity as a key).

fields.name: creatorAccountId
fields.description: The account that dispatched `create_multisig` (the event's `caller`). NULL for genesis rows.

fields.name: identityId
fields.description: denormalised — makes the identity rollup a groupBy, not a join. Null when the holder account has no known identity

fields.name: assetHolderId
fields.description: The identity's rollup for this asset; null for an account with no known identity. Re-stamped with `identity`

fields.name: amount
fields.description: fungible balance held

fields.name: frozen
fields.description: The part of `amount` the asset's agents have frozen, as the chain last set it. What the holder can move is `amount - frozen`, less any lock, so reading `amount` alone shows a balance the chain may refuse to send. The chain reports the resulting absolute value whichever call changed it, so this is replaced, never accumulated. Not summed into the identity rollup: the chain freezes a holder, never an identity

fields.name: frozenSince
fields.description: When the asset's agents froze this whole holder against transfers of the asset; null while it is not frozen. A timestamp rather than a Boolean so it can be filtered on (`frozenSince: { isNull: false }`), and unindexed because this table is already at its index limit

fields.name: nftCount
fields.description: count of non-fungible tokens held; the tokens are `nfts`

fields.name: nodeId
fields.description: A globally unique identifier. Can be used in various places throughout the system to identify this single value.

fields.name: fromPortfolioId
fields.description: `fromPortfolioId` will be null in transactions where either the Asset was issued or the sender is an account

fields.name: fromAccountId
fields.description: `fromAccount` will be populated when asset transaction has initiated directly from an account

fields.name: fromIdentityId
fields.description: `fromIdentityId` is the DID of the sender, present for transfers and redemptions. Stored separately from portfolio/account to preserve historical queryability when accounts change identity

fields.name: toPortfolioId
fields.description: `toPortfolioId` will be null in transactions where either the Asset was redeemed or the receiver is an account

fields.name: toAccountId
fields.description: `toAccount` will be populated when asset transaction has settled directly into an account

fields.name: toIdentityId
fields.description: `toIdentityId` is the DID of the receiver, present for issuances and transfers. Stored separately from portfolio/account to preserve historical queryability when accounts change identity

fields.name: amount
fields.description: `amount` is the number of fungible tokens involved in this transaction

fields.name: nftIds
fields.description: `nftIds` are the IDs of the non-fungible tokens involved in this transaction

fields.name: eventId
fields.description: denormalised: the event type consumers filter and group this table by, which aggregation cannot reach through `createdEvent`

fields.name: fundingRound
fields.description: `fundingRound` will only be present for the cases where Assets are issued with a fundingRound name

fields.name: instructionId
fields.description: `instruction` will only be present for the cases where Assets are transferred once instruction is executed

fields.name: instructionMemo
fields.description: `instructionMemo` will only be present for the cases where memo is provided for the instruction which got executed

fields.name: isInternalTransfer
fields.description: true when both sides belong to one Identity (a portfolio movement, or a settlement same-DID fast path); null for issuance and redemption. Not indexed — filter by plain equality

fields.name: memo
fields.description: note attached to a portfolio movement or a settlement.transferFunds call

fields.name: address
fields.description: the account that signed the extrinsic, for movements initiated directly by an account

fields.name: fromAccount
fields.description: Reads a single `Account` that is related to this `AssetTransaction`.

fields.name: toAccount
fields.description: Reads a single `Account` that is related to this `AssetTransaction`.

fields.name: fromIdentity
fields.description: Reads a single `Identity` that is related to this `AssetTransaction`.

fields.name: toIdentity
fields.description: Reads a single `Identity` that is related to this `AssetTransaction`.

fields.name: fromPortfolio
fields.description: Reads a single `Portfolio` that is related to this `AssetTransaction`.

fields.name: toPortfolio
fields.description: Reads a single `Portfolio` that is related to this `AssetTransaction`.

fields.name: instruction
fields.description: Reads a single `Instruction` that is related to this `AssetTransaction`.

fields.name: asset
fields.description: Reads a single `Asset` that is related to this `AssetTransaction`.

fields.name: createdEvent
fields.description: Reads a single `Event` that is related to this `AssetTransaction`.

fields.name: nodeId
fields.description: A globally unique identifier. Can be used in various places throughout the system to identify this single value.

fields.name: id
fields.description:
The chain's numeric instruction sequence, stored as text and zero-padded to 10
digits, so `orderBy: [ID_ASC/DESC]` is a total order that matches
id-assignment (chronological) order. Filter by a literal id with the padded
form, e.g. `id: { equalTo: "0000014712" }`.

fields.name: endBlock
fields.description: `endBlock` is applicable only when `type` is `SettleOnBlock`

fields.name: endAfterBlock
fields.description: `endAfterBlock` is applicable only when `type` is `SettleManual`

fields.name: tradeDate
fields.description:
The trade date, as reported by the chain. UTC, but serialised with no timezone
marker: a consumer receives `"2021-11-05T13:56:36"` and `new Date(...)` parses it
as *local* time, shifting it silently by the reader's offset. Parse as UTC — e.g.
`new Date(value + 'Z')`.

fields.name: valueDate
fields.description: The value date, as reported by the chain. UTC, serialised with no timezone marker — parse as UTC (e.g. append 'Z'), not local time

fields.name: mediators
fields.description: DID of the mediators

fields.name: legCount
fields.description: How many legs the instruction has. Their ids are `id/0` to `id/(legCount - 1)`

fields.name: rejectedById
fields.description: Who rejected the instruction: the rejection's caller, who need not be a party

fields.name: rejectedBySignerId
fields.description: The account that signed the rejection; null when there is none

fields.name: venue
fields.description: Reads a single `Venue` that is related to this `Instruction`.

fields.name: rejectedBy
fields.description: Reads a single `Identity` that is related to this `Instruction`.

fields.name: rejectedBySigner
fields.description: Reads a single `Account` that is related to this `Instruction`.

fields.description: Reads a single `Event` that is related to this `Instruction`.

fields.name: createdEvent
fields.description: Reads a single `Event` that is related to this `Instruction`.

types.name: __Schema
types.description: A GraphQL Schema defines the capabilities of a GraphQL server. It exposes all available types and directives on the server, as well as the entry points for query, mutation, and subscription operations.

fields.name: types
fields.description: A list of all types supported by this server.

fields.name: queryType
fields.description: The type that query operations will be rooted at.

fields.name: mutationType
fields.description: If this server supports mutation, the type that mutation operations will be rooted at.

fields.name: subscriptionType
fields.description: If this server support subscription, the type that subscription operations will be rooted at.

fields.name: directives
fields.description: A list of all directives supported by this server.

types.name: __Type
types.description:
The fundamental unit of any GraphQL Schema is the type. There are many kinds of types in GraphQL as represented by the `__TypeKind` enum.

Depending on the kind of a type, certain fields describe information about that type. Scalar types provide no information beyond a name, description and optional `specifiedByUrl`, while Enum types provide their values. Object and Interface types provide the fields they describe. Abstract types, Union and Interface, provide the Object types possible at runtime. List and NonNull types compose other types.

types.name: __TypeKind
types.description: An enum describing what kind of type a given `__Type` is.

enumValues.name: SCALAR
enumValues.description: Indicates this type is a scalar.

enumValues.name: OBJECT
enumValues.description: Indicates this type is an object. `fields` and `interfaces` are valid fields.

enumValues.name: INTERFACE
enumValues.description: Indicates this type is an interface. `fields`, `interfaces`, and `possibleTypes` are valid fields.

enumValues.name: UNION
enumValues.description: Indicates this type is a union. `possibleTypes` is a valid field.

enumValues.name: ENUM
enumValues.description: Indicates this type is an enum. `enumValues` is a valid field.

enumValues.name: INPUT_OBJECT
enumValues.description: Indicates this type is an input object. `inputFields` is a valid field.

enumValues.name: LIST
enumValues.description: Indicates this type is a list. `ofType` is a valid field.

enumValues.name: NON_NULL
enumValues.description: Indicates this type is a non-null. `ofType` is a valid field.

types.name: __Field
types.description: Object and Interface types are described by a list of Fields, each of which has a name, potentially a list of arguments, and a return type.

types.name: __InputValue
types.description: Arguments provided to Fields or Directives and the input fields of an InputObject are represented as Input Values which describe their type and optionally a default value.

fields.name: defaultValue
fields.description: A GraphQL-formatted string representing the default value for this input value.

types.name: __EnumValue
types.description: One possible value for a given Enum. Enum values are unique values, not a placeholder for a string or numeric value. However an Enum value is returned in a JSON response as a string.

types.name: __Directive
types.description:
A Directive provides a way to describe alternate runtime execution and type validation behavior in a GraphQL document.

In some cases, you need to provide options to alter GraphQL's execution behavior in ways field arguments will not suffice, such as conditionally including or skipping a field. Directives provide this by describing additional information to the executor.

types.name: __DirectiveLocation
types.description: A Directive can be adjacent to many parts of the GraphQL language, a __DirectiveLocation describes one such possible adjacencies.

enumValues.name: QUERY
enumValues.description: Location adjacent to a query operation.

enumValues.name: MUTATION
enumValues.description: Location adjacent to a mutation operation.

enumValues.name: SUBSCRIPTION
enumValues.description: Location adjacent to a subscription operation.

enumValues.name: FIELD
enumValues.description: Location adjacent to a field.

enumValues.name: FRAGMENT_DEFINITION
enumValues.description: Location adjacent to a fragment definition.

enumValues.name: FRAGMENT_SPREAD
enumValues.description: Location adjacent to a fragment spread.

enumValues.name: INLINE_FRAGMENT
enumValues.description: Location adjacent to an inline fragment.

enumValues.name: VARIABLE_DEFINITION
enumValues.description: Location adjacent to a variable definition.

enumValues.name: SCHEMA
enumValues.description: Location adjacent to a schema definition.

enumValues.name: SCALAR
enumValues.description: Location adjacent to a scalar definition.

enumValues.name: OBJECT
enumValues.description: Location adjacent to an object type definition.

enumValues.name: FIELD_DEFINITION
enumValues.description: Location adjacent to a field definition.

enumValues.name: ARGUMENT_DEFINITION
enumValues.description: Location adjacent to an argument definition.

enumValues.name: INTERFACE
enumValues.description: Location adjacent to an interface definition.

enumValues.name: UNION
enumValues.description: Location adjacent to a union definition.

enumValues.name: ENUM
enumValues.description: Location adjacent to an enum definition.

enumValues.name: ENUM_VALUE
enumValues.description: Location adjacent to an enum value definition.

enumValues.name: INPUT_OBJECT
enumValues.description: Location adjacent to an input object type definition.

enumValues.name: INPUT_FIELD_DEFINITION
enumValues.description: Location adjacent to an input object field definition.

args.description: Explains why this element was deprecated, usually also including a suggestion for how to access supported similar data. Formatted using the Markdown syntax, as specified by [CommonMark](https://commonmark.org/).

directives.name: specifiedBy
directives.description: Exposes a URL that specifies the behaviour of this scalar.

args.name: url
args.description: The URL that specifies the behaviour of this scalar.
